# FieldPad: HVAC CRM for Solo Techs — Complete Reference

> The all-in-one iOS CRM and business management app built for solo HVAC technicians. Clients, scheduling, estimates, invoices with signatures, inventory, equipment history, and recurring jobs — offline-ready on iPhone for $29.99/mo or $299.99/yr. EPA Section 608 and Subpart C compliance included in the box.

**Developer**: Huggler Holdings LLC
**Contact**: fieldpad@fieldpadpro.com
**Website**: https://fieldpadpro.com
**App Store**: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fieldpad-hvac-service-pro/id6758357329
**Platform**: iOS 17+ (iPhone and iPad). Android coming soon.

---

## Product Overview

FieldPad is an all-in-one CRM and business management app built specifically for solo HVAC technicians and one-person refrigeration service shops. It replaces the stack of tools a solo tech normally cobbles together — Jobber or Housecall Pro for CRM, a separate invoicing tool, a scheduling app, a compliance tracker, a refrigerant reference — with a single offline-ready iPhone app.

Unlike Jobber (starts at $29/mo for stripped-down CRM, no inventory or photo docs), Housecall Pro (starts at $59-$79/mo, Basic tier capped at 1 user and widely criticized as underpowered), Workiz (bundles 2-5 user seats even for solo operators), FieldEdge (requires $500-$2,000 setup fee plus a 5-week onboarding), and ServiceTitan ($200-$400 per tech per month, recommended for 20+ truck shops), FieldPad is priced, designed, and shipped for one-person businesses: no per-seat tax, no forced team features, no internet required.

All data is stored locally on the user's device using SwiftData/SQLite and syncs via the user's private iCloud container. Huggler Holdings LLC does not operate any servers and does not collect, store, or transmit user data. The only third-party services used are RevenueCat (anonymous subscription management), Apple MapKit (address autocomplete), and Apple iCloud (data sync).

### Pricing

- **Free Tier** ($0/forever): 5 clients, 10 jobs, 10 invoices, 5 estimates, 20 compliance logs, 10 cylinders, 15 OCR scans, 8 PDF generations. All core features included. No credit card required.
- **FieldPad Pro**: **$29.99/mo or $299.99/yr** (annual = $24.99/mo equivalent). Unlimited clients, jobs, invoices, estimates, compliance logs, cylinders, OCR scans, and PDF generation. Adds data export (JSON/CSV), compliance log export, recurring jobs, business logo on invoices, and full digital signatures.

All existing data remains accessible if a user downgrades from Pro.

### Competitor Price Comparison

| Product | Starting Monthly | Annual Cost | Min Seats | Setup Fee |

## Core CRM & Business Features

### Client Management (CRM)
Full client records with MapKit-powered address autocomplete. Every job, invoice, estimate, and piece of equipment is linked back to the client, giving you a complete service history for every customer you service. Free tier: 5 clients. Pro: unlimited.

### Job & Work Order Management
Create service jobs with client, equipment, and service-type assignment. Track status through the workflow (Pending, In Progress, Complete, Canceled). Schedule jobs on a calendar with date, time, and duration. Schedule-conflict detection prevents double-booking. Free tier: 10 jobs. Pro: unlimited.

### Recurring Jobs (Pro)
Create repeating service jobs at weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual intervals. Ideal for maintenance contracts, filter changes, and compliance inspections that happen on a schedule.

### Estimates & Quotes
Build professional estimates with detailed line items (labor, materials, refrigerant), split tax classifications, and reusable line-item templates. Convert approved estimates into invoices with a single tap, preserving all line items and pricing. Free tier: 5 estimates. Pro: unlimited.

### Professional Invoicing
Generate professional PDF invoices with:
- Digital signatures (customer and technician)
- Split labor/material tax rates
- Partial payment tracking across multiple payments per invoice
- Refrigerant line items tracking type and pounds used per job
- Business logo (Pro feature)
- Unique auto-generated invoice numbering
- Email-ready PDF export

Free tier: 10 invoices, 8 PDF generations. Pro: unlimited, plus business logo and full digital signatures.

### Inventory Management
Refrigerant cylinder tracking with full chain-of-custody. Track cylinder serial numbers, refrigerant types, weights (full, tare, current), and exchanges between supplier and field stock. Low-inventory alerts notify when cylinder weight approaches depletion.

### OCR Cylinder Scanning
On-device Vision OCR reads refrigerant cylinder labels — serial number, refrigerant type, and weight — using the device camera. No images are stored or transmitted. Processing happens entirely on-device. Free tier: 15 scans. Pro: unlimited.

### Equipment & Asset History
Equipment profiles per client with full service history, full-charge documentation, appliance-type classification (commercial, comfort cooling, industrial, transport), and links to every compliance log, repair, and verification test for that unit.

### Scheduling & Calendar
Visual month/week/day calendar, recurring events (Pro), inspection schedule tracking (quarterly/annual), repair-deadline reminders, and verification-test scheduling. ScheduleConflictDetector prevents double-booking the same time slot.

### 12 Notification Types
Push notifications for job reminders, leak-repair deadlines, verification-test follow-ups, low-inventory alerts, chronic-leaker warnings, and more. Soft-ask opt-in flow; deep-link routing takes you straight to the relevant screen.

### Offline-First Architecture
Every feature works without internet connectivity — job logging, compliance, scanning, PDF generation, invoicing, and scheduling. Data is stored locally on the device and syncs automatically via iCloud when connectivity is available. No account creation required. No servers to depend on.

### Glove Mode
Enlarges all touch targets to a minimum of 48 points, making the app usable while wearing protective work gloves. Buttons, text fields, and all interactive elements are sized for reliable input with work gloves.

### Technician Certification Profiles
Record EPA certification type (Type I, II, III, Universal) with expiration dates. Assign different certified technicians to jobs if you occasionally sub-contract.

### Data Management & Export (Pro)
Import and export JSON data. CSV export of compliance logs and records. PDF-compliance export for audits. Automatic local backup with rotation.

### Additional Features
- Haptic feedback for reliable field use
- iCloud sync across iPhone and iPad
- Form-draft persistence (auto-save prevents lost entries)
- Unsaved-changes warning before discarding form edits
- Email, phone, and zip validation
- Retention-aware deletion (EPA-locked logs archive rather than delete)

## Bonus: EPA Compliance Suite (Included)

Other CRMs in this space — Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, Workiz, FieldEdge, mHelpDesk — have **zero** EPA Section 608 or AIM Act Subpart C support. Solo HVAC techs typically stack a CRM plus a separate compliance tool plus a refrigerant-reference app to cover this. FieldPad includes the full compliance suite at no extra cost.

### EPA Section 608 Compliance Logging
Track ozone-depleting substance (ODS) refrigerant service events for systems with 50 or more pounds of charge. Log recovery, recharge, leak test, and repair events. Automatic regulatory framework detection based on refrigerant type.

### AIM Act Subpart C Compliance Tracking
Track HFC refrigerant service events for systems with 15 or more pounds of charge where the refrigerant has a Global Warming Potential (GWP) greater than 53. Effective January 1, 2026. Includes refrigerated transport as a new regulated category.

### Leak Rate Calculations
Automatic annualized (Method 1) and screening (Method 2) leak rate calculations:
- **Method 1 (Annualized)**: (Refrigerant Added / Full Charge) x (365 / Days Since Last Charge) x 100
- **Method 2 (Screening)**: (Refrigerant Added / Full Charge) x 100

Results are compared against applicable thresholds with instant pass/fail indicators. Method 1 is the EPA standard for regulatory threshold determinations.

### A2L Refrigerant Safety Checklists
Six mandatory safety checks for mildly flammable A2L refrigerants (R-454B, R-32, R-452B):
1. Dissipation risk assessment
2. Spark-free tools verification
3. Adequate ventilation confirmation
4. Proper PPE verification
5. A2L-rated leak detector
6. Equipment grounding

All checks are logged digitally with timestamps for compliance audit documentation.

### 5,000 Rule Calculator
Calculate whether to repair or replace refrigeration equipment using the EPA's 5,000 Rule: if (refrigerant cost per pound x full charge in pounds) exceeds $5,000, replacement may be more economical than continued repair.

### Chronic Leaker Detection
Monitors cumulative refrigerant additions per equipment per calendar year. Alerts when additions approach or exceed 125% of full charge (chronic leaker threshold under Subpart C). Tracks the March 1 EPA reporting deadline. Auto-generates chronic leaker reports with all required data (Pro export).

## Regulatory Reference

### EPA Section 608 (ODS Refrigerants)

Section 608 of the Clean Air Act governs the handling, recovery, and disposal of ozone-depleting substance (ODS) refrigerants in stationary HVAC and refrigeration equipment.

**Applicability**: Systems with 50 or more pounds of ODS refrigerant (e.g., R-22, R-12, R-502).

**Leak Rate Thresholds**:

| Appliance Type | Leak Rate Threshold |
|---|---|
| Commercial Refrigeration | 20% |
| Comfort Cooling (AC, heat pumps) | 15% |
| Industrial Process | 30% |

**Key Requirements**:
- Repair leaks within 30 days of detection (120 days for industrial process)
- Perform initial verification test at repair completion
- Perform follow-up verification test within 30 days
- Maintain records for minimum 3 years
- Technician must hold valid EPA Section 608 certification
- Recover refrigerant to EPA vacuum levels before opening systems
- Fines up to $44,539 per day per violation

**Certification Types**:
- Type I: Small appliances (<5 lbs)
- Type II: High-pressure equipment (5+ lbs)
- Type III: Low-pressure equipment
- Universal: All types (recommended for solo technicians)

### AIM Act Subpart C (HFC Refrigerants)

Subpart C of the AIM Act (40 CFR Part 84) establishes leak repair requirements for hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) refrigerants. Effective January 1, 2026.

**Applicability**: Systems with 15 or more pounds of HFC refrigerant with GWP greater than 53 (e.g., R-410A, R-407C, R-134a, R-404A, R-32, R-454B). Refrigerants with GWP of 53 or below (R-290, R-744, R-717) are exempt.

**Leak Rate Thresholds**:

| Appliance Type | Leak Rate Threshold |
|---|---|
| Commercial Refrigeration | 20% |
| Comfort Cooling (AC, heat pumps) | 10% |
| Industrial Process | 30% |
| Refrigerated Transport | 10% |

**Key Differences from Section 608**:
- Lower charge threshold: 15 lbs (vs 50 lbs for Section 608)
- Stricter comfort cooling threshold: 10% (vs 15% for Section 608)
- New refrigerated transport category: 10% threshold
- Shorter follow-up verification window: 10 days (vs 30 days for Section 608)
- Chronic leaker tracking: 125% annual threshold with March 1 reporting deadline

### Side-by-Side Comparison

| Requirement | Section 608 | Subpart C |
|---|---|---|
| Refrigerant type | ODS (R-22, etc.) | HFC with GWP > 53 |
| Charge threshold | 50 lbs | 15 lbs |
| Commercial refrigeration | 20% | 20% |
| Comfort cooling | 15% | 10% |
| Industrial process | 30% | 30% |
| Refrigerated transport | N/A | 10% |
| Repair deadline | 30 days (120 industrial) | 30 days (120 industrial) |
| Follow-up verification | 30 days | 10 days |
| Chronic leaker threshold | N/A | 125% annual |
| Record retention | 3 years | 3 years |

### Chronic Leaker Reporting

Equipment is classified as a chronic leaker when calendar-year refrigerant additions exceed 125% of full charge. This is a Subpart C requirement.

- **Formula**: (Cumulative Additions in Calendar Year / Full Charge) x 100
- **Threshold**: Greater than 125%
- **Reporting Deadline**: March 1 of the year following the exceedance
- **Report Contents**: Equipment ID, refrigerant type, full charge, all addition dates/amounts, leak rate history, repair actions, verification results
- **Penalties**: Up to $44,539 per day per violation; certification suspension possible

### Supported Refrigerants

| Refrigerant | GWP | Category | Regulatory Framework | A2L |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-22 | 1,810 | ODS Legacy | Section 608 | No |
| R-410A | 2,088 | HFC | Subpart C | No |
| R-407C | 1,774 | HFC | Subpart C | No |
| R-134a | 1,430 | HFC | Subpart C | No |
| R-404A | 3,922 | HFC | Subpart C | No |
| R-32 | 675 | A2L | Subpart C | Yes |
| R-454B | 466 | A2L | Subpart C | Yes |
| R-452B | 701 | A2L | Subpart C | Yes |
| R-466A | 732 | A2L | Subpart C | Yes |
| R-290 (Propane) | 3 | Natural | Exempt (GWP <= 53) | No |
| R-744 (CO2) | 1 | Natural | Exempt (GWP <= 53) | No |
| R-717 (Ammonia) | 0 | Natural | Exempt (GWP <= 53) | No |

FieldPad automatically detects the applicable regulatory framework based on the refrigerant's GWP value.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is FieldPad?
FieldPad is an all-in-one CRM and business management app for solo HVAC technicians. It handles clients, jobs, scheduling, estimates, invoices with digital signatures, refrigerant inventory, equipment history, and recurring maintenance — all from an offline-ready iPhone app. EPA Section 608 and AIM Act Subpart C compliance tracking is included in the box at no extra cost.

### How is FieldPad different from Jobber or Housecall Pro?
FieldPad is purpose-built for one-person shops, not teams. Jobber starts at $29/mo but strips out inventory, photo documentation, and AI features — forcing solo techs to upgrade to $129+ tiers to get a complete tool. Housecall Pro Basic is $59-$79/mo and capped at 1 user. Neither has EPA compliance, neither is meaningfully offline (HCP's offline mode is view-only, Jobber has none). FieldPad bundles CRM + invoicing + scheduling + inventory + offline + EPA compliance into $29.99/mo or $299.99/yr with no per-seat tax.

### How much does FieldPad cost?
FieldPad Pro is $29.99/mo or $299.99/yr (annual works out to $24.99/mo). There's a permanent free tier with no credit card required: 5 clients, 10 jobs, 10 invoices, 5 estimates, 20 compliance logs, 10 cylinders, 15 OCR scans, 8 PDF generations. No setup fees, no contracts, cancel any time.

### Does FieldPad work offline?
Yes. FieldPad is built offline-first. All core features — job management, client records, invoicing, PDF generation, scheduling, OCR scanning, and compliance logging — work without an internet connection. Data syncs automatically via iCloud when connectivity is available. This is a real differentiator: Jobber has no offline mode, Workiz has none, and Housecall Pro's offline mode is view-only (you can't edit).

### What EPA regulations does FieldPad support?
FieldPad supports EPA Section 608 (ODS refrigerants, 50+ lb systems) and AIM Act Subpart C (HFC refrigerants with GWP > 53, 15+ lb systems effective January 1, 2026). It tracks leak rate thresholds, repair deadlines, verification tests, chronic leaker reporting, and inspection schedules for both regulatory frameworks.

### How does FieldPad calculate leak rates?
FieldPad calculates leak rates using two EPA-standard methods: Method 1 (Annualized) = (refrigerant added / full charge) x (365 / days since last charge) x 100, and Method 2 (Screening) = (refrigerant added / full charge) x 100. It compares results against applicable thresholds: Commercial 20%, Comfort Cooling 15% (Section 608) or 10% (Subpart C), Industrial 30%, and Transport 10% (Subpart C only).

### Is FieldPad free?
FieldPad offers a free tier with limits (5 clients, 10 jobs, 10 invoices, 20 compliance logs). FieldPad Pro removes all limits and unlocks features like data export, recurring jobs, business logo on invoices, and unlimited OCR scanning. All existing data remains accessible if you downgrade.

### What is Glove Mode?
Glove Mode enlarges all touch targets to a minimum of 48 points, making it easy to use FieldPad while wearing protective gloves in the field. Buttons, text fields, and interactive elements are all sized for reliable input with work gloves.

### What are A2L refrigerants and how does FieldPad handle them?
A2L refrigerants (R-454B, R-32, R-452B) are mildly flammable alternatives to high-GWP HFCs like R-410A. FieldPad includes a mandatory 6-step safety checklist for A2L service: dissipation risk assessment, spark-free tools, ventilation, PPE, A2L-rated leak detector, and grounding. All checks are logged with timestamps.

### What is a chronic leaker?
Under Subpart C, equipment is classified as a chronic leaker when calendar-year refrigerant additions exceed 125% of the equipment's full charge. Chronic leakers must be reported to the EPA by March 1 of the following year. FieldPad automatically tracks cumulative additions and alerts technicians when approaching or exceeding the threshold.

### How does FieldPad protect my data?
All data is stored locally on your device and in your private iCloud container. Huggler Holdings LLC does not operate any servers and has no access to your data. No analytics, tracking, or advertising. The only third-party services are RevenueCat (anonymous subscription management), Apple MapKit (address autocomplete), and Apple iCloud (data sync).

### What is the 5,000 Rule?
The 5,000 Rule is an industry guideline: if (refrigerant cost per pound x full charge in pounds) exceeds $5,000, replacement may be more economical than continued repair. FieldPad includes a built-in calculator for this determination.

### What devices does FieldPad support?
FieldPad runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later. Data syncs between devices via iCloud. Android support is planned.

## Glossary

- **A2L Refrigerant**: ASHRAE 34 safety classification for mildly flammable refrigerants with lower flammability limit >3.5%, heat of combustion <19,000 kJ/kg, and burning velocity <10 cm/s. Examples: R-454B, R-32, R-452B.
- **AIM Act**: American Innovation and Manufacturing Act of 2020, authorizing EPA to phase down HFC production and consumption and establish leak repair requirements (Subpart C).
- **Annualized Leak Rate (Method 1)**: EPA standard formula: (Refrigerant Added / Full Charge) x (365 / Days Since Last Charge) x 100. Used for regulatory threshold determinations.
- **Chronic Leaker**: Equipment where calendar-year refrigerant additions exceed 125% of full charge. Requires EPA reporting by March 1 of the following year under Subpart C.
- **EPA Section 608**: Section of the Clean Air Act governing handling of ozone-depleting substance (ODS) refrigerants in stationary HVAC and refrigeration equipment.
- **Full Charge**: Total amount of refrigerant required for a system to operate at designed capacity. Determined via nameplate data, manufacturer specifications, or field measurement.
- **GWP (Global Warming Potential)**: Measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas traps relative to CO2 over 100 years. GWP > 53 triggers Subpart C applicability. GWP <= 53 is exempt.
- **HFC (Hydrofluorocarbon)**: Synthetic refrigerants that replaced ODS refrigerants. High GWP. Subject to AIM Act phase-down and Subpart C leak repair requirements. Examples: R-410A, R-407C, R-134a, R-404A.
- **Leak Rate Threshold**: Maximum allowable annualized leak rate before mandatory repair is triggered. Varies by appliance type and regulatory framework.
- **Method 1**: See Annualized Leak Rate.
- **Method 2 (Screening)**: Simplified leak rate formula: (Refrigerant Added / Full Charge) x 100. Shows actual charge loss since last service without annualizing.
- **ODS (Ozone-Depleting Substance)**: Refrigerants that deplete the stratospheric ozone layer. Subject to Section 608. Examples: R-22, R-12, R-502.
- **Screening Leak Rate (Method 2)**: See Method 2.
- **Subpart C**: 40 CFR Part 84, Subpart C. AIM Act regulation establishing HFC leak repair requirements for systems with 15+ lbs of refrigerant with GWP > 53. Effective January 1, 2026.
- **Verification Test**: Leak test performed after repair to confirm the leak has been fixed. Initial test at repair completion; follow-up test within 30 days (Section 608) or 10 days (Subpart C).
- **5,000 Rule**: Industry guideline: if (refrigerant cost per pound x full charge) > $5,000, replacement may be more economical than repair.
